thread:
anya: Quick Q — trying to connect the SDK to an internal/private endpoint behind a corporate proxy. I set REDWOOD_API_BASE to the internal hostname and HTTPS_PROXY to our proxy, but I get TLS handshake errors or 403s. Anyone seen this pattern?

sam: Which SDK/lang and are you using mutual TLS for the private control plane?

anya: Node (js SDK 0.9.2). Yes mTLS. Env: REDWOOD_API_BASE=https://internal-rw.example.local, HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.corp:3128. Failures are immediate TLS errors or streaming cuts out mid-response.

sam: Common issues: proxy can break SNI/host header, or it doesn't support CONNECT tunneling for streams. For Node you can override the servername used for TLS (fixes SNI mismatch) and pass client cert/key to the agent. Example (rough):

```js
const fs = require('fs');
const https = require('https');
const agent = new https.Agent({
  ca: fs.readFileSync('/secrets/ca.pem'),
  cert: fs.readFileSync('/secrets/client.crt'),
  key: fs.readFileSync('/secrets/client.key'),
  servername: 'internal-rw.example.local' // force SNI/host
});

const client = new RedwoodClient({
  baseUrl: process.env.REDWOOD_API_BASE,
  httpAgent: agent,
  proxy: process.env.HTTPS_PROXY // or let the environment handle it
});
```

sam: That servername override often fixes TLS handshake issues when the proxy rewrites SNI to the proxy host.

maria: If you're on Python, same idea — use SSLContext and set server_hostname in wrap_socket or set hostname in create_default_context. Also check whether the proxy is doing TLS termination (corporate MITM) — then you need the proxy CA in your CA bundle.

kevin: Streaming-specific note: many corp proxies buffer or do not support HTTP/1.1 chunked streaming unless you use CONNECT. If streaming disconnects, try forcing tunnel mode for API traffic or use a direct route (no_proxy) for the internal host.

anya: Is there a recommended env var/placement for the client certs? I currently tried REDWOOD_CLIENT_CERT_PATH & REDWOOD_CLIENT_KEY_PATH but the SDK didn't pick them up automatically.

sam: The SDK will auto-read REDWOOD_CLIENT_CERT and REDWOOD_CLIENT_KEY (PEM blobs) if provided. For path based, load them yourself and pass into the client options (see agent example). We purposely avoid reading arbitrary file paths by default for security/consistency.

maria: Also double-check Host header — some proxies replace Host with the proxy host. If the private endpoint validates Host, you can set explicit header in the SDK request: headers: { 'host': 'internal-rw.example.local' } — but only if your proxy allows header passthrough.

kevin: For retries/backoff: streaming calls are not idempotent, so keep retries off for streaming. For regular requests, set:

```js
{ retries: 3, backoff: { factor: 2, min: 200, max: 2000 } }
```

kevin: And add an idempotency key header for retriable operations that modify anything on the server.

anya: Great — one more: the corporate proxy requires client cert auth too. Will dual mTLS (client->proxy and proxy->internal) break anything?

sam: You can have mTLS on both legs but watch cert selection: the proxy will authenticate your client cert; the proxy then mTLS to the internal service (separate cert). On Node you must configure the tunneling agent to present the client cert on the CONNECT to the proxy. Example using tunnel/https-proxy-agent to pass cert/key to the proxy.

maria: TL:DR checklist: 1) try no_proxy for internal host, 2) if proxy required -> use CONNECT/tunneling, 3) force SNI/servername to internal host, 4) add proxy CA to trust store if proxy terminates TLS, 5) pass client certs into agent explicitly, 6) avoid retries on streaming.

anya: Awesome, will try these. Thanks! :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: reminder: do NOT commit certificates or keys to repo — use secrets manager (vault/aws-sm) and mount into runtime. :lock:
